newsitem.title: USA: STG/MARK TO RIDE OUT CABLE STORM--U.S. TECHNICIANS.
newsitem.headline: STG/MARK TO RIDE OUT CABLE STORM--U.S. TECHNICIANS.

text.p: Cable's one-month shakeout gathered momentum on Thursday but a robust dollar/mark will probably cushion the blow to sterling/mark, technical analysts said.
"Sterling could come off hard, dollar/mark could rally strong and sterling/mark could just hang right around in here," said Ture Johnson, technical analyst at Bank of America.
The pound violated key support in the form of a March 18 bottom at $1.5850 on Thursday on its way to a 10-month low at $1.5780, chartists said.
The slide only stalled as cable neared the 61.8-percent retracement of the rise from $1.4888 in May 1996 to the December high at $1.7163, which comes in at 1.5760.
Analysts said the retreat confirmed a major double-top pattern, defined by the monthly peak at $1.7163 coupled with July's $1.6986 zenith.
"There is a lot of gloom and doom on this currency over next couple of months given this double-top pattern," said Ben Morden, a technical analyst at I.D.E.A. Inc.
"Short-term, we may see some more selling toward $1.56 to $1.54 but ultimately ... you would have to think towards $1.50 $1.4885," Morden said.

Sterling/mark on Thursday also broke through key support at the July 29 bottom at 2.9723. While a daily close below this level could spell trouble, ending below 3.00 marks on a weekly basis or 2.96 for one day would be far greater cause for alarm, chartists said.
"Closing below 2.9730 is going to be bearish," Johnson said. "A close below 2.96 would confirm the break and we should get down to the 2.95 to 2.94 area, at a mimimum."
At 1200 EDT on Thursday, the pound was at $1.5870/80, down from $1.6028/38 at Wednesday's U.S. close and near 2.9670 marks, compared to around 3.0180.
